_doc: Where each agent CLI keeps a session's transcript, and WHERE IN THAT PATH THE
⛔ `icon_kind` IS THE SPELLING A ROW REPORTS, AND IT IS NOT ALWAYS THE SLUG.
A codex row's `icon_kind` is the historical `session`, which ships on the wire
and may not be renamed. A resolver that matched a row's kind against these KEYS
therefore never narrowed for codex — 410 of 742 live rows on 2026-08-22 — and
fell through to trying every declared store, which was right only by luck.
`session_kind_for_row` in yggterm-core is the one owner of this question and
the Rust lock makes it ratify every alias here.
SESSION ID SITS — the one thing the fleet verbs need that the CLI registry does
not already publish on a row.
⛔ THIS FILE IS NOT A SECOND COPY OF THE REGISTRY. `store_globs` is transcribed
from `AgentCliDescriptor::session_store_globs` and is checked against it by
`the_fleet_transcript_table_matches_the_registry` in yggterm-core, which FAILS
the build if the two drift. The registry stays the owner of where a store is;
this file adds only the id position, expressed as `{id}` inside the glob.
⚠ Every template here was resolved against a REAL store, not a fixture: a genuine
session id taken from disk, substituted in, and required to return exactly the
file it came from. A CLI with no store, or one whose store has never been seen on
a real machine, says so rather than guessing — an unverified template that looks
plausible is the failure this whole area keeps repeating.
`verified_on_disk` means exactly that and nothing weaker.

codex.note: The file name DECORATES the id with a timestamp, so the id is a suffix.

codex-litellm.note: Same layout as codex under its own root; no session on any host reached.

claude-code.note: The only store whose file name IS the id. Every verb assumed this shape.

pi.note: Timestamp prefix, underscore, then the id.

qwen-code.note: ⛔ UNVERIFIED AND THE ONLY ONE THAT LOOKS WRONG. 27 sessions across two hosts hold ONLY `<id>.runtime.json` sidecars — a pid/cwd marker with no title and no conversation — and zero `.jsonl` files. Every one of them was an unauthenticated probe that never exchanged a message, so this cannot yet be told apart from `a transcript appears only once a session says something`. Settle it by authenticating this CLI and running ONE exchange; until then neither this template nor the registry's live reader has been shown to resolve a real session.

muse.note: The id names the session's DIRECTORY; every file inside is named the same.

antigravity.note: The id names a directory several levels above the file, and every session's file has the SAME name — which is why slicing a row's path for its id collapsed five rows onto one. The `.db` in the store is a summaries index, not the transcript.

grok-build.note: Sits under a URL-ENCODED cwd directory, so the parent cannot be derived.

opencode.note: Declares no store in the registry. Nothing to resolve, and saying so is the honest answer — a guessed path here would read as measured.

kimi.note: kimi 1.50.0 moved the store BACK to ~/.kimi (md5-of-cwd buckets, bare-uuid session dirs, NO state.json) — the 0.27-era .kimi-code/state.json glob here was dead and the gate test failed until this row caught up ([11.104]; registry owner: session_store_globs = .kimi/sessions/*/*/wire.jsonl per the 11.6.6-a c-tail landing, context.jsonl deliberately unmatched). The session id is the bare-uuid directory; verified 2026-09-14 against a live store by substituting the real id 373af60b-0dc8-42e6-848a-23c5ee8a31c1 into this template and matching its wire.jsonl exactly.

zcode-tui.note: The file NAME is the id, whole: model-io-<session-uuid>.jsonl. One rollout file per session; the session title lives in the shared store (.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite session.title). Measured 2026-09-07 against the zcode-tui campaign sessions on a fleet host.

devin.note: MEASURED 2026-09-16 (devin-battery suite on 3000.10.27, 8/8 twice live): the store is ONE SQLite db, ~/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db (WAL; tables sessions/prompt_history/message_nodes/rendered_commits/tool_call_state/subagent_heads/app_state). Session ids are word-word SLUGS (scythe-snowplow); sessions.title = the first prompt (eager self-titling); a row exists only for a COMPLETED turn - a turnless session leaves session_locks/<slug>.lock (pid) and no row. Transcripts live inside the db (message_nodes), so there is no per-session transcript PATH to declare - empty globs are the SHAPE (opencode posture), not a gap.

mimo.note: MEASURED-PARTIAL 2026-09-26 (mimo intake on the muse lab host, 0.1.15): the store is ONE SQLite db, ~/.local/share/mimocode/mimocode.db (WAL; session/project/permission/claude_import/... tables). Session ids are ses_... (opencode law); title + title_source present at row creation (eager, 'fallback'); timestamps epoch-ms. Transcripts live inside the db - empty globs are the SHAPE (opencode/devin posture). HAZARD: first launch AUTO-IMPORTS Claude Code sessions (claude_import table) so ses_ rows exist for conversations mimo never ran.
